battle.name: 王仙芝起義
battle.brief: 乾符二年（875）河南大饑，鹽商王仙芝聚饑民於曹、濮、宋、兗之間起兵，三年轉戰十餘州，兵眾由數萬增至十餘萬，逼近汴洛而終未下洛陽。僖宗招撫與討伐並用皆無效，仙芝終以兵變死於潞州，部眾歸於黃巢。卡面的秦連弩正係唐軍守城壓制攀城者的利器。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 這場戰爭的一方是唐王朝的中央與方鎮聯軍，另一方是王仙芝在河南道聚起來的饑民與亡命之眾。唐僖宗李儇在位時，天下分為數十道，軍政財權由各道節度使分割，河東、河南、兗鄆、忠武、宣武諸鎮各自募兵置將，遇亂則各自守境，中央號令往往不出河南道。仙芝起義的區域正落在河南道腹地：曹州、濮州、宋州、亳州一帶是鹽井與漕運交會之地，州縣城郭完整、府兵已廢、募兵久闢，守方倚城自固，討方則只能靠各鎮臨時調發的兵與客軍。叛軍方面並無正式編制，起義初期是饑民結隊，攻城之後收攏散卒、降卒與亡命，漸漸以仙芝為核心合編，人數由數萬增至十餘萬，但裝備與糧秣全靠就地和劫掠供給。僖宗一方則以宣撫招撫為先、討伐為後：先遣使散財誘降，失敗之後才命兗鄆節度使張軍陀、宣武軍節度使王忠嗣、昭義軍節度使孟方立等分道出擊。結果是征討軍彼此不相協、各守封疆，叛軍反而得以在數州之間流動作戰；這種中央與藩鎮之間的裂縫，正是這場戰爭能夠延續三年的結構性原因。
countriesEn: One side of this war was the Tang court together with the armies of the regional military governors, and the other was the hungry population and the fugitives that Wang Xianzhi had gathered in Henan Circuit. When Emperor Xizong of Tang, Li Xuan, held the throne, the empire was divided into dozens of circuits, and military, political and fiscal power was carved up by the jiedushi of each. The circuits of Hedong, Henan, Yanzhou-Yong, Zhongwu and Xuanwu each raised their own soldiers and appointed their own commanders; when trouble broke out every circuit simply guarded its own borders, and the orders of the central court seldom carried beyond Henan. The theatre of Xianzhi's rising lay in the belly of Henan Circuit: Cao, Pu, Song and Bo, where salt wells met the canal transport routes. The prefectures and counties still possessed walls, but the fubing militia had long been abolished and the recruited armies had stood idle for years, so the defenders could only rely on their walls, and the punitive side could count on nothing but troops hastily sent out by the circuits together with mercenary retinues. The insurgents had no formal establishment at all. In the first months they were simply bands of starving peasants; after taking towns they absorbed scattered soldiers, surrendered men and runaway criminals, and gradually a single core formed around Xianzhi. Their numbers grew from several tens of thousands to over a hundred thousand, yet their arms and food depended entirely on what they could take locally or seize by plunder. The Tang side led with pacification and followed with arms: envoys were sent first with money and gifts to buy the rebels back, and only when that failed did the court order the jiedushi Zhang Juntao of Yanzhou-Yong, Wang Zhongsi of Xuanwu and Meng Fangli of Zhaoyi to strike from separate directions. The result was that the punitive armies did not cooperate with one another, each guarding its own fief, while the insurgents were free to move and fight between prefectures. That structural fracture between the court and the regional militaries is the reason this war could run for three years.
people: 王仙芝是這場戰爭的主角。他出身河南道鹽商家庭，熟悉鄉里道路與物價行情，通曉騎射而好談兵事，平日以錢財交遊州縣吏員，好以兵事自炫，遇饑民聚眾為亂便乘勢而起，成為首領。他用人不疑但賞罰不常，隊伍成份雜，既有真為求食的饑民，也有趁亂求財的盜匪；起義初期連破州縣、殺官吏、掠倉場，靠的是出其不意與流動性，而非任何攻城器械上的優勢。黃巢是曹州冤句人，世代以鹽為業，聞仙芝起兵便遣其弟率眾來會，兩股力量此後一直並立而不相統屬，直到仙芝死後才合為一軍。僖宗李儇怠於朝政，信任宦官田令孜，把榷鹽與軍需供應一併交給內府，亂起之後只能靠加派與招撫維持軍費。將帥方面，兗鄆節度使張軍陀是少數真正追擊仙芝的宿將，曾在羊馬城一線追奔破敵；宣武軍節度使王忠嗣奉命討平，受命日久而進度遲緩；昭義軍節度使孟方立掌握潞州，兵敗之後一度以州城降仙芝。中下層的叛軍首領尚復、尚讓、查莊等人則在仙芝死後爭奪兵柄：尚復在軍中譁變殺仙芝，尚讓、查莊收攏餘眾與黃巢會合，另有名為蔡宗杜的部將率眾降唐。
peopleEn: Wang Xianzhi was the protagonist of this war. He came from a family of salt merchants in Henan Circuit, knew the roads and the price of grain in every market town of his native district, was at home on horseback and with the bow, and talked endlessly about warfare. He spent his money cultivating officials in the prefectures and counties and boasted of his military talents; when famine drove the people into disorder he rose with them and became their leader. He trusted his men easily but was erratic in rewards and punishments, and the composition of his bands was mixed, including genuine famine victims as well as bandits who had joined for plunder. His early successes in storming prefectures, killing officials and emptying the granaries rested on surprise and mobility rather than on any advantage in siege engines. Huang Chao was a native of Yuanju in Caozhou, whose family had long lived on salt; when he heard that Xianzhi had risen he sent his younger brother with troops to join him, and the two forces remained parallel and unsubordinated to each other until they merged into one army after Xianzhi's death. Emperor Xizong, Li Xuan, was negligent in state affairs and trusted the eunuch Tian Lingzi, handing over the salt monopoly and the supply of military stores to the inner palace; once disorder began he could keep the army supplied only by additional levies and by pacification. Among the generals, Zhang Juntao, jiedushi of Yanzhou-Yong, was one of the few who genuinely pursued Xianzhi and broke his men in the field near the Yangma walled town; Wang Zhongsi, jiedushi of Xuanwu, was ordered to put the rising down but advanced slowly; Meng Fangli, jiedushi of Zhaoyi, held Lu prefecture and after defeat offered that city to Xianzhi. Among the insurgent commanders of lower rank, Shang Fu, Shang Rang and Zha Zhuang fought over the command after Xianzhi died: Shang Fu mutinied and killed him, Shang Rang and Zha Zhuang gathered the survivors and joined Huang Chao, and a commander named Cai Zongdu led a body of men over to the Tang side.
kits: 卡面這件秦連弩是弩機把拉力儲存起來、一踩一發的連發弩具，源於戰國，墨家《公輸》篇已論其守城之用，曹魏諸葛亮又加以損益，後世沿襲為城頭常備的守城火器。及至唐朝，連弩並未淘汰，反而與角弓弩、稍弩、擘張弩並列為官府兵仗的骨幹：擘張弩需兩人張弦、拉力以石計，是野戰與守城的中距離主力；角弓弩輕便，適合守軍轉向追擊；連弩則架在城垛與城門兩側的射孔之後，以連發的箭壓制貼牆攀爬的攻方，把一次一發的射擊壓力攤成持續不斷的覆蓋。唐軍野戰裝備以明光鎧、札甲與長柄刀槊為主，騎兵比例在河南、江淮一線仍相當高，軍中同時攜帶角弓與馬弓箭壺；攻城一方可用的器械包括投石機、雲梯與飛雲梯、撞竿、火箭與猛火油，但唐末州縣城防因經費不足而普遍失修，許多城郭只有土築圍牆與女牆，連弩一類射擊器械的儲備遠不如州治所屬的緊要關口齊備。這場起義的攻城多為輕兵夜襲、穴地掘進與突門，器械消耗遠小於中原會戰，故連弩的價值主要體現在防禦一端：官軍據城拒守的成敗，相當程度上取決於城頭連弩的射速與箭矢存量能否壓住四面同時上來的攻城者。連弩在唐代的細節仍散見於敦煌文書所載的弩具清冊與各地出土的唐代銅弩機殘件，具體形制仍有待考古資料逐步補全。
kitsEn: The Qin repeating crossbow on the card face is a weapon whose trigger mechanism stores the draw power so that one press of the lever looses one bolt; it goes back to the Warring States period, when the Mohist text Gongshu already discussed its use in the defence of walls, and Zhuge Liang of Cao Wei later modified it, after which it remained in use as a standing wall-top weapon. By the Tang dynasty the repeating crossbow had not been displaced; it stood alongside the horn bow crossbow, the light crossbow and the heavy-drawn crossbow as a backbone of official military stores. The heavy crossbow, drawn by two men and rated in stone, was the mid-range backbone in the field and in defence; the horn bow crossbow was light and handy for a defending garrison that had to swing its aim; the repeating crossbow, set up behind the crenellations and the arrow slits beside the city gates, poured a stream of bolts at men already clinging to the wall, turning the pressure of a single shot into unbroken coverage. Tang field equipment rested on bright armour plates, lamellar armour and long-handled sabres and spears, the proportion of cavalry in Henan and along the Yangzi was still high, and the army carried both the horn bow and the bow case for horse archery. The attacking side could bring stone-throwers, siege ladders and flying ladders, battering poles, fire arrows and fire oil. The walls of Tang prefectures and counties, however, were generally out of repair for want of funds, many being earth ramparts with a parapet only, and stocks of fire weapons such as the repeating crossbow were far thinner in the smaller prefectures than at the strategic passes. In this rising the storming of towns was done by light troops at night, by tunnelling and by seizing the gates, and so the wear on siege engines was much less than in a pitched battle on the plain. The value of the repeating crossbow therefore lay on the defensive side: whether a Tang garrison could hold its wall depended in large measure on whether the rate of fire and the stock of bolts on the ramparts could cover attackers pressing in from four sides at once. The details of the Tang repeating crossbow survive in the lists of crossbow equipment found among the Dunhuang documents and in the fragments of bronze trigger mechanisms recovered from Tang-period sites, and its exact form is still being filled in by archaeological evidence.
tactics: 叛軍在三年之中沒有一次正面攻擊大城正面的戰役，行動方式近乎標準的流動游擊：白日偃旗息鼓、鼓噪擾敵，入夜分隊銜枚疾行，天明之前撲向目標州縣的城門或四面鄉鎮；得手即縱兵搜括倉廩、驅畜而去，不作久屯，因此唐軍雖有城池可守，卻難以確定敵蹤；無法追擊，敵去兵又散於荒野。仙芝本人善於用賄結交州縣吏員，攻城之前常先通款，約定內應或買通守門者，再以精銳銳卒登門，成功則裡應外合奪門，失敗則立刻退走，不作攻堅。攻不下便改打別處，州縣互相不能相救，因為各鎮節度使只求保境自守，不願他鎮出兵配合，這使叛軍得以在曹、濮、宋、亳、兗、沂之間逐次轉戰。與之相對的官軍戰術則以據城死守為主：兗鄆節度使張軍陀部與宣武軍節度使王忠嗣部在羊馬城一線合擊，斷其糧道，再乘其饑疲追奔至陶家川一帶，才迫使仙芝部眾潰散；但此類成功只在多鎮協同之處出現，一旦各軍分兵，城與城之間的呼應仍然斷裂。叛軍的崩潰同樣出在戰術層面：糧秣不繼而州縣已空，軍中易生譁變，仙芝病死軍中隨即被部將所殺，正是因為隊伍已無共同的目標可以維繫。
tacticsEn: In the three years of the rising there was not a single pitched assault on the face of a great walled city; the method of the insurgents was close to textbook mobile harassment. By day they kept their flags furled and beat drums to make noise and disturb the enemy; by night they moved in small columns with their mouths plugged, and before dawn they fell on the gates of the target prefecture or on the villages around it. On success they swept the granaries, drove off the livestock and left again without making a long camp, so that the Tang army, though it owned the walls, could hardly track the enemy; unable to pursue, it saw the rebels dissolve into the fields. Xianzhi himself was skilled at cultivating local officials with money. Before a storming he often sent word ahead, arranging for an inside accomplice or buying the gate guards, and then led picked troops through the gate; on success the town was taken by action from within and without, and on failure he withdrew at once rather than grinding on. When a town could not be taken he struck somewhere else, because the prefectures could not help one another: each jiedushi wanted only to preserve his own circuit and would not commit troops to a neighbour, and this allowed the rebels to move in turn among Cao, Pu, Song, Bo, Yan and Yi. The Tang tactics, by contrast, were to hold the walled city and fight to the death. The troops of Zhang Juntao of Yanzhou-Yong and those of Wang Zhongsi of Xuanwu came together in the line of Yangma, cut the rebels' supply road, and then exploited their hunger to chase them back as far as the Taojia stream, and only such combined operations forced the followers of Xianzhi to scatter; once the armies were separated, the mutual support of city by city broke down again. The collapse of the insurgents also happened at the tactical level: with the grain route broken and the towns emptied, mutiny was easy, and Xianzhi, dying in his camp, was killed at once by his own commanders precisely because the army no longer had a common purpose to hold it together.
data: 可核的數字並不多，而且各史記載互有出入，此處只列比較可靠以及明確存疑者。起義初期的人數，諸書有「聚眾數千」「萬餘」「數萬」三說，較可信的說法是乾符二年（875）河南饑民成群結隊，王仙芝以數千人為骨幹，到年底已能攻破亳州，兵力增至數萬；乾符三年至四年之間眾至十餘萬，一說數十萬，則顯有誇大。乾符四年（877）羊馬城與陶家川方向的戰鬥，通行記載稱官軍斬首萬餘級、追奔數十里，此類數字在晚唐史書中多有浮報，不宜當作實際殘殺量。仙芝在乾符五年（878）七月病歿於潞州時，其眾尚有數萬；其後蔡宗杜率眾降唐者以萬計，餘眾多併入黃巢麾下，數字各書記載亦無定論。器械方面，弩在唐代已有明確等級：一石約合今一百二十斤，擘張弩拉力逾千斤而需兩人張弦，其有效射程在二百至三百步之間；單兵角弓弩射程稍近而操作快捷；連弩的優勢在射速，同一射手可比擘張弩多出數倍發數，卻受制於弩機零件的損壞與箭矢存量。作戰距離方面，仙芝部眾在曹州至宋州、亳州至兗州、兗州至蘄州之間的轉戰，多在三百至六百里的地面上完成，靠的是輕裝與沿途劫糧，所以史書常記其行軍數百里而糧不給。至於雙方總傷亡數，現存史料沒有可靠的統計。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked are few, and the records disagree with one another, so only the better supported figures and the openly doubtful ones are set out here. For the strength of the rising at its opening the histories give three versions, several thousand, more than ten thousand, and tens of thousands; the more credible account is that in 875 the famine victims of Henan gathered in bands, that Wang Xianzhi used some thousands as the skeleton of his force, and that by the end of the year he was strong enough to storm Bo prefecture with a force grown to several tens of thousands. Between 876 and 877 his numbers reached above one hundred thousand, while the claim of several hundred thousand is plainly exaggerated. For the fighting along the Yangma and Taojia lines in 877 the received account gives more than ten thousand heads cut off and a pursuit of several dozen li; figures of that kind are commonly inflated in late Tang histories and should not be read as an actual body count. When Xianzhi died of illness at Lu prefecture in the seventh month of 878 he still had several tens of thousands under him; after his death the men who came over to the Tang under Cai Zongdu were counted in thousands, while the remainder was absorbed into Huang Chao's command, and again the sources give no settled figure. On weapons, the crossbow had clearly graded ranks in the Tang: one stone was about one hundred and twenty catties, the heavy crossbow needed two men to draw it and pulled with a force above a thousand catties, and its effective range lay between two hundred and three hundred paces; the single-man horn bow crossbow had a shorter range but could be handled far more quickly. The advantage of the repeating crossbow lay in rate of fire, a single archer loosing several times as many bolts as a heavy crossbow could, though it was limited by the wear of the trigger parts and by the stock of bolts. On distances, the marching of Xianzhi's men from Cao to Song, from Bo to Yan, and from Yan to Qi was carried out over ground of three hundred to six hundred li, achieved by light order and by taking grain along the way, which is why the histories so often note armies marching several hundred li without food. As for total casualties on both sides, the surviving sources contain no reliable statistics.
cause: 起義的直接導火線是乾符元年（874）河南道的大水與饑荒。河南是唐廷的軍糧產地與漕運樞紐，鹽法又以榷鹽專賣把大量小民逼入私販，一旦遇上災年，農民既失田產又無官糧可賴，饑民成群結隊流入州縣，盜劫、掠倉、殺吏的事層出不窮。朝廷的處置不是賑災而是防範：既沒有足夠的常平倉與義倉糧食下放，又怕地方官擅自出粟，只好改用招撫與賞格，試圖用金帛買回秩序。仙芝正是利用了這一點：饑民願意跟隨能帶來糧食與安全的人，而鹽商的財貨、人脈與對鄉里的熟悉，正好可以提供這些。他起兵之後，僖宗一面命將討伐，一面又下詔招撫，授以州刺史與將軍名號，企圖用官爵換取解散，結果是招撫與討伐交替，叛軍既未解散也未受創，反而在兩者之間越戰越強。深層的背景是懿宗以來藩鎮割據與軍鎮私鬥，中央財政被各鎮截留，禁軍逃亡與邊兵潰散者流入河南，成為叛軍最現成的兵源；同時宦官田令孜控制榷鹽與軍需，加派苛急，天災與人禍疊加，於是八世紀末的河南，成為整個唐王朝最先崩解的地區。
causeEn: The immediate trigger of the rising was the great flood and famine that struck Henan Circuit in 874. Henan was the Tang court's granary and the pivot of its canal transport, and the salt regulations, which reserved the trade as a monopoly, had already pushed a great many small folk into smuggling; once a bad harvest year came the peasants lost both their fields and any prospect of official grain, starving bands poured into the prefectures and counties, and robbery, plunder of the depots and the killing of officials followed one another. The court's answer was not relief but containment: with neither the ever-normal granaries nor the charitable granaries able to release enough grain, and with fear that local officials would give out store grain on their own initiative, the only instrument left was pacification and reward, an attempt to buy the peace back with money and silk. Xianzhi exploited exactly this: famine victims would follow anyone who could bring them food and safety, and a salt merchant's cash, connections and familiarity with the countryside could supply precisely that. Once he had risen, Xizong ordered his generals to attack and at the same time issued edicts of pardon, granting titles of prefectural governor and general in the hope of buying the bands back into the fields; the result was that pacification and attack alternated, the rebels were neither dissolved nor checked, and grew stronger in the gap between the two. The deeper background was the fragmentation of the empire into autonomous militaries since the reign of Emperor Yizong and the private wars between them, with central revenue intercepted at every circuit: deserters from the imperial guards and soldiers disbanded on the frontier drifted into Henan and became the most ready source of recruits for the rebels. At the same time the eunuch Tian Lingzi controlled the salt monopoly and military supply and levied heavy surtaxes, and natural disaster piled on top of man-made oppression, so that by the close of the eighth century Henan had become the first region of the Tang state to come apart.
impact: 王仙芝起義是唐朝末年第一次大規模的地方民變，它改變了此後十餘年的戰爭格局。第一，州縣城防體系暴露了致命弱點：唐廷在河南的駐軍以節度使私兵為主，中央對各鎮只有虛名，討逆之師彼此猜防、寧可坐失戰機也不願併力，叛軍卻能以流動游擊的方式連續作戰，兩年之間轉戰十餘州，逼得朝廷屢換將帥。第二，招撫為主的政策在此後被證明無效，從仙芝到黃巢，朝廷先撫後剿、剿而復撫的老路重複了兩次，等到黃巢兵鋒直指兩京，廷中仍舊有人力主招安，幾乎是同一套劇本的第三次上演。第三，河南的鹽業、漕運與賦稅秩序崩壞，軍需無著，戰亂由河南推向關中，最終導致廣明元年（880）黃巢入長安、僖宗奔蜀，兩京陷落。從技術層面看，這場戰爭也是晚唐城防與軍械的一次大規模實地檢驗：州縣普遍缺兵少械、器械不修，防守方最終仍舊回到「弩加城牆」的保守辦法；連弩這類射速極高的守城器械雖無從普及到每一座州城，其設計思路卻在此後的城防論述中一直被反覆提及。王仙芝本人則成為唐末藩鎮與亂軍之間過渡的典型人物——他既非純粹的亂民，也非朝廷倚重的藩鎮，他的結局預示了後來方鎮以討亂為名、擁兵自重、終至割據的走向。
impactEn: The Wang Xianzhi rising was the first large-scale local rebellion of the late Tang, and it changed the shape of the following decade or more of war. First, it exposed a fatal weakness in the system of walled-town defence. The troops the court held in Henan were in practice the private armies of the jiedushi, and central authority over the circuits was nominal. The punitive armies distrusted one another and would rather lose a chance than combine their efforts, while the rebels could fight a continuous war of mobile harassment, passing through more than ten prefectures in two years and forcing the court to replace its commanders again and again. Second, the policy of meeting rebellion with pacification was shown to be useless. From Xianzhi to Huang Chao the court walked the same road twice, pacifying and then attacking, attacking and then pacifying again, and by the time Huang Chao's spearhead pointed at the two capitals there were still voices in court urging a negotiated surrender, which was very nearly the same script performed for a third time. Third, the salt trade, the canal transport and the fiscal order of Henan broke down, the army could not be supplied, and the fighting moved out of Henan into Guanzhong, ending with Huang Chao's entry into Chang'an in 880 and Xizong's flight to Shu, the two capitals falling in turn. At the level of technique, this war was also a great field test of late Tang fortification and ordnance: the prefectures and counties were short of men, short of arms and short of repaired equipment, and the defensive side fell back on the conservative formula of a crossbow on top of a wall. Fire weapons of the repeating crossbow's speed could not be made universal in every prefecture, yet the idea behind them kept being raised in later discussions of city defence. Xianzhi himself became the typical transitional figure between the late Tang militaries and the rebel bands: he was neither a pure populist nor a governor the court could rely on, and his end foreshadowed the course by which the circuits would raise troops under the pretext of stamping out disorder, hold them for their own profit, and end up carving out independent principalities.
result: 乾符五年（878）七月，王仙芝在攻圍潞州的戰役中病重，部將尚復等人趁軍中譁變，將他殺死並割取首級送與黃巢；仙芝一死，他用三年時間聚起來的聯軍立即分崩：部將尚讓、查莊收攏餘眾與黃巢會師，眾仍以數萬計，兵權從此歸入黃巢之手；另有部將蔡宗杜率眾降唐，朝廷照例授以州刺史一類官爵以為瓦解之策，但真正被收編進攻勢的不是唐軍而是叛軍自身。仙芝在三年裡沒有攻下洛陽、汴州任何一座大城，最後攻破的只有山東、河南的中小州縣與湖北蘄州；他所造成的破壞，主要是把河南道各州的城防、府庫與戶口消耗殆盡，使中央在黃巢兵鋒抵達之前就已失去再整軍、再籌糧的餘力。追討仙芝的官軍同樣沒有勝績：兗鄆節度使張軍陀在羊馬城、陶家川一線追奔的戰果隨仙芝之死而落空，其後更被黃巢大軍所殺，昭義軍節度使孟方立一度以潞州降仙芝，說明唐廷對河南道各鎮的約束已近乎名存實亡。就全局而言，王仙芝起義並非以任何一方的決定性勝利告終，而是以叛軍首領的猝死、其部眾被另一支更大的叛軍吸收、唐朝的討逆體系被消耗殆盡而收場；從此以後，唐末的亂局不再是個別州縣的民變，而成為席捲關中、江南與河東的全面崩解。
resultEn: In the seventh month of 878, while he was besieging Lu prefecture, Wang Xianzhi fell gravely ill, and his commanders such as Shang Fu mutinied in the camp, killed him, cut off his head and carried it to Huang Chao. With Xianzhi dead, the coalition he had assembled over three years fell apart at once: commanders such as Shang Rang and Zha Zhuang gathered the survivors and joined Huang Chao, the host still numbered tens of thousands, and the command passed into Huang Chao's hands. Another commander, Cai Zongdu, led his men over to the Tang, and the court as usual granted him a title of prefectural governor in the belief that this would break up the rest; but the force that was really absorbed into the offensive was not the Tang army but the rebels themselves. In three years Xianzhi never took either of the great cities of Luoyang or Bian. What he did capture were only the smaller prefectures and counties of Shandong and Henan and the prefecture of Qi in Hubei, and the destruction he caused lay mainly in wearing out the walls, the treasuries and the households of the Henan prefectures, so that the centre had no strength left for re-forming its troops or gathering its grain before Huang Chao's spearhead arrived. The Tang armies sent against him were no more successful. The work of Zhang Juntao of Yanzhou-Yong, who had chased Xianzhi along the Yangma and Taojia lines, was undone by Xianzhi's death, and Zhang himself was later killed by Huang Chao's great army; Meng Fangli, jiedushi of Zhaoyi, had already offered Lu prefecture to Xianzhi, which showed that the court's hold over the circuits of Henan existed in little more than name. On the whole the rising did not end in a decisive victory for either side. It ended with the sudden death of the rebel leader, the absorption of his followers by a larger rebel army, and the exhaustion of the Tang apparatus for suppressing revolt. From that point the disorder of the late Tang was no longer the uprising of individual prefectures and counties but a general collapse spreading across Guanzhong, Jiangnan and Hedong.
